item.title: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight: "Monster House" (placeholder nickname) Looking For Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The main SCP a dingy old house that periodically teleports from one place to another, usually in the middle of woods, or abandoned areas. You can't see in the windows, and opening the door reveals a black void leading to another dimension. Within the void is a race of bipedal, dragon like creatures (SCP-XXX-1) that can shapeshift. They typically take the form of human children and wander the woods asking people to help them find their parents. They then take the victim to the house and abduct them into the void, no one who has entered has ever come out.

Central Narrative: will include mission logs detailing the first encounter with the SCP, and an attempted recovery of one of the creatures. After capturing the creature, it is discovered that they disappear if they go further than 1km away from the house. This information, along with another piece of info, leads to some theorizing that the house may have been built to trap the entities inside, rather than the entities using it as a pathway to our dimension.

Hook: The hook is mainly how creepy the idea is, having a child come up to you in a forest and asking you to help them find their parents, only to turn into a dragon creature and take you into an endless black void.

Additional Notes: I have a mostly completed article on my sandbox, just needs the encounter log, some proofreading, and some streamlining.

item.title: SCP concept - The Artist: Re: SCP concept - The Artist
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I have some questions and opinions about your concept that hopefully will help you develop this concept into a more unique and appealing one.

First off, the idea of an artist capable of giving life to his creations is absolutely not new, it not only has been done before but also there is a whole group of interest composed by anomalous artists. You may want to take a look at the "Are We Cool Yet?" article on the GoI tab here at the forum (I'm on mobile so forgive me for not linking it here)
However, I don't think you should scrap off this idea just yet. Think of how this artist could be different from others, you said he knows many techniques, maybe focus on one art and elaborate on how he does it and how it affects/is affectes by his anomaly. For example, an artist that can only sculpt but can use any material to do so: air, water, volcanic lava. Also, what kind of person is this artist? Does he know how to use his anomalous abilities? Is he aware of them?

As I said, there is potential but it's still quite basic and generic. I hope you find a way to make it more special and unique :)

item.title: Greenlight Request: A Second Reflection: Greenlight Request: A Second Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.

It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.

It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment.

Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.

At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs (Edited and revised): Re: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs (Edited and revised)

Like cybersqyd I think this gets a bit over the top… I like the idea of the weird kitchen with faceless chefs… and then I lose all interest when its a #scary door that is forbidden and the chef kills the agents…

I genuinely suggest you take a different tack here. Simplify the anomaly to being the faceless chefs, making good food anomalously… and then expand that aspect. Don't shift it to scary door and scary paranoia other worlds. Sit and consider the weirdness of an anomalous kitchen that makes normal but excellent food.

I think there's a story there.

item.title: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System: Re: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
ok. I am willing to GREENLIGHT this, but I am going to warn you that this doesn't seem to be a strong narrative.

A few nitpicks:

+ show block
– hide block

This:

This is part of the reason I intend to add the audio file, not just for the story/narrative, but for the sound effects the skip makes, (cracking, sloshing, banging, skittering, etc.) and the scientist's reactions, which I think will add to the discomfort factor (I know audio is what made SCP-682 so infamous, not that my intention is to mimic that article).

Does not address my concern below:

so just a gory description of this anomaly isn’t really story rich, or all that unique

Body horror is very common on the wiki (suggest you look at Sarkicism Hub) so even if the audio is gross and the description is gross… that's not a story. For example, have you seen any slasher horror movies? Impressive gory violence isn't exactly a story beat… its meant to shock

What I am saying is: DONT rely only on the body horror to make your article work. Do more than imply characterization, because without something to relate to… the reader will just think "gross" and maybe that'll work for some but just as likely it won't work for others.

The second addendum mentions that other researchers heard the whisper, describing it as an indiscriminate noise, and recommended further research in case it meant something (without mentioning what the whisper said, or that it was even a whisper).

If I am not mistaken, we (as the readers) will hear this whisper in the audiofile, yes? So if we can understand it, how would 2 separate researchers be unable to recognize speech?

The origin is implied in the description section. I mention the shrunken portions of the brain that control cognition, motor functions, memory, etc, without explicitly stating their function- it just says frontal lobe, parietal lobe, and hippocampus without explaining to the reader why that's significant; I don't intend to talk down to them.

To me, this would not imply that the fetus took the mother's brain. A fetus has a brain I think… or a protobrain like organ that is developing.

Essentially it's a downer ending as the skip can't get what it wants, despite its hardships. Because its still technically alive at the end, it's left open-ended, though. Do you think it should not be open-ended?

I think "open ended" can be good. This does not seem open-ended, it seems shallow of facts/plot. I think you need to expand this in terms of the narrative… why would the child do this? Why would this have happened at all? Why should the Foundation care at all?

item.title: The Shield that Redirects its Damage: Re: The Shield that Redirects its Damage
item.content:encoded:
PM request acknowledged, time for a followup! :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: An Indian shield from the 16th century that has connection to the 3 main Hindu gods. When held by a living person with the belief of doing heroic deeds will cause a blue energy field to cover it and tempt them to do said heroic deeds. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). If its wielder has villainous or wrongful ideas then the shield will be corrupted and its energy field will turn red, fueling its wielder's ideas.

Overall, I don't have much of an issue with the concept, you seem to have a strong grasp on what the skip is. My only main issue with the concept is the the skips overall purpose, as it doesn't seem to be expanded upon much. which in turn makes the concept feel a bit flat.

The current focus: "if you're good then the shield will be blue, and you do good things. And if you're bad the shield will be red, and you do bad things", is a bit of cliche as it feels like it's just making the wearer a super hero or super villain without bringing anything new in.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The shield came to the foundation's attention when reports of a man wielding a glowing blue shield was committing vigilantism in India. An investigation was initiated as several agents were sent to recover it. They were able to subdue the vigilante, but once they removed the shield his body crumbled to dust only leaving behind his equipment and some notes. In the process of being taken to the Foundation it ended up causing some trouble along the way as it switched between blue and red when held by different personnel, causing suspicion and conflict among them. Once finally contained, tests are conducted on the shield and the notes are analyzed to learn more about it.

I quiet liked where the story was going with the suspicion between personnel, but that avenue just sort of stopped abruptly in favour of testing the skip, which made the payoff feel anticlimactic.- what came of the suspicions? who were these characters? what interventions did they have? whats everything building up to?

Along with this, I feel the setup could be stronger as currently the original wearer just sort of feels like a plot device for the Foundation, as he doesn't really contribute much to the narrative, or give any sort of insight into the skip. Rather, he just disappears with no context or development, which feels like a quick way to get out of writing character interactions, especially since the "crumbling into dust" isn't mentioned before or after this.- why does this happen? does the Foundation ever get an any context to this? do they research it? why isn't it mentioned again? what did the "vigilante" actually do?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

-I would recommend focusing your narrative more around the suspicions between characters, and the shields way of showing "good" and "bad".

Also, try to keep away from just turning the wearer's into super heroes (or villains) as it makes the concept feel cliched and hard to get invested in, as characters are much more complex than just "good" or "bad", what where the characters intentions? who were they? why should I as reader care about them? what is considered "good" and "bad" ect.

If you would like any additional feedback, feel welcome to send me a PM :) I look forward to any further edits! and if you're looking for any new perspectives or other critters in general, I would highly recommend the butterfly squad.

Cheers,

RED

item.title: SCP Greenlight Request "The Toybox": Re: SCP Greenlight Request "The Toybox"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (thinking Euclid Clas)

Genre: Weird Tales/Horror

Page Layout: N/A

Elevator Pitch: An antique toybox may not be as harmless as it appears.

Central Narrative: The item in question is an antique toybox, constructed of seasoned, naval grade wood and secured with pig iron fittings. It features an integrated locking mechanism, and is not unlike a seachest in construction.

The toybox contains a variable number of toys appropriate to its size. Toys can vary when a box has been locked and unlocked, but will otherwise remain the same in everyday use.

The locking and unlocking process is somewhat disquieting. In order to be unlocked, the individual physically turning the key must be an individual twelve years of age or younger OR such an individual must be present within the room.

In order to -lock- the box, the individual turning the key must be an adult (aged eighteen years or older). Furthermore, all items that were discovered within the box must have been removed, and then returned.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Each of the toys might seem harmless enough, but was in fact in its time notoriously unsafe. Where historically appropriate, the item may have been recalled. This might include items such as: a lazertag set with ultra-realistic guns; a batman cape which, when worn, tends to convince the wearer they can glide safely from a height to ground; a bag of marbles that look very much like candy; a set of lawn darts;etc.

Additional Notes: The toybox is incredibly old. Notes will indicate spectrographic analysis showing use at least as far back as the early eighteenth century.

item.title: SCP Greenlight Request "The Toybox": SCP Greenlight Request "The Toybox"
item.content:encoded:
Elevator Pitch: An antique toybox of considerable age may be far more dangerous than it initially appears.

Summary: While I've written up more extensive details, I understand this is just the pitch, so, here we go. I don't -think- this idea has been used yet, though with 4,000+ articles, I could very much be wrong.

The item is an antique toybox, high quality wood with pig iron fittings, with an integral locking function. One, and only one, key has been found to work. Can be freely opened and closed when not locked. When unlocked, may only be locked by an adult, with a few additional requirements. When unlocked, may only be unlocked by a "child" (12 or younger), or when such an individual is present in the room.

The contents vary somewhat, but always contain a selection of toys, which may be freely removed by anyone once the box is unlocked. They consist of examples from a broad swathe of history, but have one thing in common: all are toys that are notoriously dangerous to children, many of which have been recalled. All are examples that have occurred within our own reality. Ie:

  • The notorious Battlestar Galactica toy whose missile firing mechanism caused a child to choke to death.
  • The Barbie doll whose sparking rollerblades caused fires.
  • A "lazertag" set circa 1985 that makes it appear that the players are using real guns, presenting an alarming scene to law enforcers. (this resulted in shooting deaths in the 1980s)
  • A set of large plastic "conkers" attached to elastic strings that can damage a child when used enthusiastically.
  • A bag of marbles that look very much like candy
  • A children's "Russian Roulette" Game
  • A Teddy Ruxpin whose tapes, when played backward, give terrible advice to children ("Let's play with Daddy's Guns!" "Let's open Mommy's Liquor Cabinet")
  • A cape from a prominent superhero franchise (historically based upon the 1960s Batman television series) that makes the wearer feel as if they can glide to earth from garage roofs, the tops of buildings, etc.

I imagine this would be a Euclid class object, requiring minimal maintenance but careful observation. Occasionally, new toys will appear, old toys will disappear, but those will invariably show up again depending upon the individual in question.

Thanks for your time!

-Alex
